text: SGLP.L is essentially dead money — sitting 99% off its 52-week high with a relative strength near rock bottom, meaning almost everything else in the market is outperforming it, so it's time to exit and free up that capital.
RGTI's revenue is shrinking by 34%, the company is deeply unprofitable, short interest is high at 15%, and it's sitting 52% below its peak — this isn't a dip worth holding through, cut the loss now.

RDW is down 23% with negative earnings, negative cash flow, 18% short interest, and four straight earnings misses — reduce your exposure here because the fundamentals keep deteriorating with no sign of a turnaround.

SKYT is up 72% and sitting at its 52-week high, but momentum just turned bearish on MACD and the company is deeply unprofitable — consider locking in some of that impressive gain before the pullback takes it away.
Meta at a PE of just 16.5 with 22% revenue growth and a streak of earnings beats makes it arguably the cheapest mega-cap tech name out there — adding here on strength makes sense.

Lockheed Martin's PE of 16, steady revenue growth, strong 5.8% free cash flow yield, and low short interest make it a reliable defense holding worth building up during a supportive rate-easing environment.
Microsoft at a PE of 23 with 15% revenue growth, consistent earnings beats, and MACD turning bullish is showing fresh upward momentum in a rock-solid business — a good spot to add shares.
RTX trades at a reasonable PE of 23 with solid revenue growth and positive free cash flow in a defense sector that continues to benefit from rising global spending — worth adding to your position.
